newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call market dormant, gilt prices rally.
newsitem.headline: Indian call market dormant, gilt prices rally.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 0.10-0.50 percent on reporting Friday, unchanged from the day's opening levels, dealers said.
"There was very little activity in the market, most of the deals were in the range of 0.10 to 0.25 percent and some stray deals at 0.50 percent," a dealer said.

Securities prices rose by 10 to 15 paise for short-dated securities. The market was acting favourably on the cash reserve ratio cut announced by the central bank and the rally is likely to continue in the coming fortnight, dealers added.

The 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded at 11.98 percent aganist Thursday's yield of 12.07 percent and 13.50 percent 1998 stock was at 12.76 percent compared to Thursday's yield of 12.88. The price of 13.62 percent 1998 rose by 15 basis points from Thursday's level to 101.95, a dealer said.
The zero coupon bonds maturing in 1999 were traded at 74.98 rupees on Friday, up from Thursday's 74.63 rupees, he added.
He said the treasury bills maturing in January 1997 were traded in a range of 8.95-9.07 percent, while October 1997 tresury bills were traded in region of 11.90-12.00 percent.

Inter-corporate deposits were quoted at 17-19 pecent for 90 days, dealers said. Commercial papers were quoted at 13.5-14.5 for P1+ companies and certificates of deposit were quoted at 12.5-14.0 percent on Friday, he said.
